title: Scanner noise curation & evidence collector playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for reducing scanner noise (false positives/low-confidence findings), standardizing the evidence payload we attach to remediation tasks, and producing a deterministic SIEM export / audit-log-friendly schema. It ties into RBAC v2 constraints for who can access remediation evidence and delineates minimal patch SLA handling when exceptions are required.

Scope:
- Static and dynamic scanner outputs ingested by vuln pipeline (OSS deps, container scans, infra-as-code, SCA).
- Evidence collector microservice (evidence-collector) that attaches artifacts to Jira tickets and forwards summarized payloads to the SIEM.
- RBAC v2 constraints for evidence access.
- SLA & escalation matrix for patching.

TL;DR action items (next 2 sprints):
1) Implement scanner confidence bucketing and debounce logic in vuln-ingest (owner: Diego).
2) Add evidence-collector field: "verification_steps" and attach: raw-scan-output, repro-commands, risk-justif, affected-repos (owner: Priya).
3) Ship SIEM CSV/JSON export mapping spec and add tests in security-scripts (owner: Kenji).
4) Draft short RBAC policy doc for Evidence Access (owner: Maya).

Background / problem statement:
- We get a high volume of scanner alerts (Snyk/Trivy/DependencyTrack) that overwhelm SEV owners. Many are noise: heuristics or infra drift bits.
- Lack of consistent evidence attached to remediation tickets causes repeated back-and-forth with eng teams.
- SIEM ingest schema is inconsistent (field names vary by scanner) so SOC runbooks can't reliably correlate indicators.
- Some evidence contains secrets or PII; RBAC v2 must prevent overexposure while still enabling SOC responders.

Definitions & glossary:
- noise: findings with low-confidence score OR high false-positive history for a specific scanner/rule combination.
- verification_steps: minimal steps to reproduce or confirm a finding (command + environment).
- evidence-collector: service that gathers artifacts from scanners, stores them in evidence-bucket and attaches metadata to tickets and SIEM payloads.

Scanner noise curation heuristics (proposal):
1) Confidence bucketing: bucket scanner findings into HIGH/MED/LOW using scanner confidence + historical FP rate for the rule.
   - HIGH: score >= 0.8 OR rule FP_rate < 0.05 and severity >= high
   - MED: 0.4 <= score < 0.8 OR FP_rate between 0.05-0.2
   - LOW: score < 0.4 OR rule FP_rate > 0.2
2) Debounce policy: require >= 2 unique scanner runs (different CI jobs or timestamps separated by >=24h) for MED/LOW before auto-create ticket.
3) Auto-suppress list: curated list of rule IDs with proven noise history (maintained by SecOps). Auto-suppress is reversible and shown on ticket.
4) Context enrichment: before marking as HIGH, gather runtime/context (image digest, IaC line numbers, callstack snippet). If enrichment fails, mark MED and require human triage.

Evidence payload schema (flat key/value form for ticket attachment and SIEM export):
- evidence_id: UUID
- finding_id: scanner-provided id (string)
- scanner: string (e.g., trivy, snyk, deptrack)
- scanner_version: string
- detection_time: ISO8601
- confidence_bucket: HIGH|MED|LOW
- severity: CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFO
- description: short text (one paragraph)
- affected_asset: string (repo/image/instance)
- affected_location: file:path or package@version or image:tag
- affected_commit: SHA (if available)
- repro_command: single-line command to reproduce (shell escaped)
- raw_output_url: signed S3 URL (or internal object id)
- snippet: sanitized excerpt (<= 8k chars)
- remediation_suggestion: short text
- evidence_collector_version: semver
- retention_tier: short|long (policy for how long to keep raw evidence)

Notes on schema: keep it flat to make SIEM mapping straightforward. Avoid embedding arrays as deep objects; arrays allowed but prefer comma-separated strings if possible to pass into legacy CSV exporters.

Audit log / RBAC considerations (RBAC v2):
- RBAC roles: sec-analyst, sec-ops, eng-owner, infra-owner, auditor (read-only).
- Evidence access matrix:
   - raw_output_url: only visible to sec-ops and eng-owner for 30 days; auditors get redacted snippets.
   - repro_command: visible to eng-owner and sec-analyst (repro only if marked non-secret). Evidence-collector must redaction-scan commands for secrets.
   - snippet & description: visible to all roles.
- RBAC enforcement points:
   - evidence-collector service signs pre-signed URLs with short TTL (default 7 days) and includes access control metadata in audit log.
   - Audit log lines for evidence access must include: user_id, role, evidence_id, action (view/download), timestamp, ip, justification_token (if manual override).

Audit log schema (flat, SIEM-friendly):
- event_id: UUID
- ts: ISO8601
- actor_id: email or service principal
- actor_role: role
- action: string (e.g., evidence:view, evidence:download, ticket:create)
- target_evidence_id: UUID
- target_finding_id: string
- method: web|api|pre-signed-url
- outcome: success|denied|error
- ip: string
- location: geo string (if available)
- justification: short text (optional)
- trace_id: correlating request id

SIEM export mapping guidance:
- Export both evidence summary (compact) and audit log lines. SIEM team prefers JSON lines but can accept flattened CSV with header mapping.
- Required SIEM fields: event_id, ts, actor_id, actor_role, action, target_evidence_id, target_finding_id, outcome, severity, confidence_bucket, affected_asset, scanner.
- Example JSON line (compact):
  {
    "event_id":"e-12345","ts":"2026-07-15T13:02:10Z","actor_id":"mchen@redwood.ai","actor_role":"sec-analyst","action":"evidence:view","target_evidence_id":"ev-0987","target_finding_id":"TRV-2026-887","outcome":"success","severity":"HIGH","confidence_bucket":"HIGH","affected_asset":"api-gateway:sha256:abcd","scanner":"trivy"
  }

Evidence automation flow (end-to-end):
1) Scanner run produces findings -> vuln-ingest normalizes -> assigns confidence_bucket and enrichment triggers.
2) For HIGH findings: auto-create ticket in Jira with evidence summary and attach raw_output_url (short TTL). For MED: put into Review queue (Slack alert to triage-shift). LOW: store as historical telemetry only and surface via periodic report.
3) evidence-collector saves artifacts into evidence-bucket with retention tag, creates evidence record in metadata DB, and attaches evidence_id to Jira ticket.
4) SIEM exporter reads metadata DB and audit logs and emits JSON lines to kafka topic siem.vuln.evidence -> SOC pipeline.

Patch SLA & exception process (proposal):
- Default SLA by severity (calendar days from ticket creation):
  - CRITICAL: 3 days (escalate to oncall sec + infra after 24h)
  - HIGH: 14 days (escalate to eng manager after 7 days)
  - MEDIUM: 45 days
  - LOW: 90 days
- SLA exceptions: must include exception justification, compensating controls, and an explicit expiration date. Exceptions create a special audit log entry and require approval by sec-ops lead.
- If patching is delayed, evidence-collector emits weekly SLA breach summary to the vulnerability dashboard and triggers PagerDuty for CRITICAL outstanding beyond 24h.

Remediation tracking / ticket fields recommended (Jira template):
- Summary: [scanner] short description - affected_asset
- Description: include evidence_id, snippet, repro_command, remediation_suggestion, links to infra PRs
- Labels: scanner:trivy|snyk, confidence_bucket:HIGH/MED, sla:CRITICAL/HIGH/etc
- Custom fields (flat strings): evidence_id, scanner_version, affected_commit, remediation_eta, exception_flag
- Component: owning-service/team

Dependency review notes (SCA specifics):
- For OSS dependency findings, attach BOM (Bill of Materials) artifact (generated by SBOM pipeline) and mark transitive vs direct. If finding is transitive, require triage to check if direct upgrade fixes it; otherwise, mark for track-and-monitor.
- For package-manager advisories, evidence-collector should add fixed_versions array (comma-separated) and link to vendor advisory.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Debounce window: 24h may delay valid infra-wide changes (e.g., vulnerable base image). Consider special-case for image-sweep findings to bypass debounce.
- Retention policy: storing raw outputs for 90 days costs money; need to map to retention_tier policy (short for transient infra findings, long for supply-chain and compliance evidence).
- Redaction heuristics: how aggressive should the secret-scan be on repro_command? False negatives here are risky.

Appendix: quick checklists
- Evidence collector checklist before attaching raw_output_url:
  - [ ] redaction scan run (secrets and PII)
  - [ ] minimum repro_command present OR link to CI job
  - [ ] BOM attached for dependency findings
  - [ ] retention_tier set
- SIEM export test checklist:
  - [ ] JSON lines valid against schema validator
  - [ ] sample event contains actor_role and action fields
  - [ ] correlation tests using trace_id work end-to-end

Meeting notes (2026-07-22 sync):
- Priya: will prototype evidence-collector v0.2 that includes repro_command redaction and retention tags.
- Diego: will add FP-rate computation to vuln-ingest and surface per-rule history in admin UI.
- Kenji: to deliver SIEM mapping and write exporters to kafka topic.
- Action: create SEC-521 to track RBAC policy doc for evidence access (Maya).

Todo / immediate next steps:
- [ ] Diego: PR for confidence bucketing (due 2026-08-01)
- [ ] Priya: evidence-collector schema PR and storage retention defaults (due 2026-07-30)
- [ ] Kenji: SIEM export unit tests and kafka wiring (due 2026-08-05)
- [ ] Maya: RBAC v2 short doc and sample audit log lines for SOC (due 2026-07-29)

References and useful links:
- Confluence: Evidence Automation Design (linked above)
- Jira: SEC-412 (vuln ingestion), SEC-521 (evidence RBAC)
- GitHub: security infra PRs (see linked_artifacts)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep playbook deliberately pragmatic; prefer incremental wins (debounce + minimal evidence fields) rather than perfect coverage.
- When in doubt, prefer exposure minimization (short-lived URLs, redaction) — SOC can request escalated access but that action must be auditable.

End of doc.
